subject: Vendor evidence harmonization: OneTrust & Vendr (CAIQ / SIG mapping)
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Vendor evidence harmonization: OneTrust & Vendr (CAIQ / SIG mapping)

Hi Neha,

We're getting ready for Greenfield's annual vendor security review and our compliance team asked whether you can help us harmonize the CAIQ/SIG answers currently split between OneTrust and Vendr. The problem we're trying to avoid: duplicate evidence uploads and inconsistent answers across portals during the audit.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood provide a single CAIQ->portal mapping file (manifest) so we can push the same canonical artifacts into both OneTrust and Vendr?
- We need an auditable proof-of-possession for certain S3-hosted artifacts (SOC 2 report, KMS-signed syslog samples).
- Preferred upload window: next Tue (2027-09-07) morning (US-EST).

I can share a list of the required documents (SOC2-summary.pdf, syslog-sample.tar.gz, key-rotation.csv). If possible, include an MD5/SHA256 checksum and a signed manifest indicating who uploaded each artifact and when.

Thanks — Oliver
Security Operations, Greenfield Health

Attachments: caiaq-request-list.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor evidence harmonization: OneTrust & Vendr (CAIQ / SIG mapping)

On Wed, Sep 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenfieldhealth.com> wrote:
> We're getting ready for Greenfield's annual vendor security review...

Hi Oliver,

We can take this on. Proposed approach (high level):
1) Redwood will produce a canonical CAIQ->portal mapping spreadsheet and a signed manifest (SHA256 + KMS signature) that references each artifact filename and checksum. We'll upload the artifacts to a temporary, KMS-protected S3 bucket and provide pre-signed URLs to your OneTrust and Vendr intake endpoints.
2) For audit traceability we'll include: uploader email, KMS key id, timestamp (UTC), and an HMAC proof included in signed-manifest.json. That manifest will be stored in the evidence folder in both portals.
3) We'll coordinate a 2-hour upload window to avoid rate-limit retries and ensure all artifacts land with the same object version id.

Ben, Marissa — can you confirm the S3 lifecycle + presign policy we should use, and whether we can create an ephemeral bucket for Greenfield with a 30-day TTL? Monica — please prepare the CAIQ mapping draft (I started a sheet in the shared Drive).

Oliver — if that matches your compliance needs, confirm the upload window and we'll send the manifest and presign links 24 hours in advance.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: caiaq-mapping-v1.xlsx (draft)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T15:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Vendor evidence harmonization: OneTrust & Vendr (CAIQ / SIG mapping)

Neha / team,

Quick follow-up on the upload mechanics:
- We'll stand up an ephemeral S3 bucket: redwood-gfh-evidence-20270907 (30-day TTL, object lock disabled).
- KMS key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 (we'll use for server-side encryption + sign the manifest).
- Presign policy: 24-hour expiration for pre-signed URLs. I'll generate a batch of URLS and include them in the signed-manifest.json along with SHA256 checksums.
- For large files (syslog tarball) we'll provide multipart-presigned POST instructions to avoid 403s and speed. See attached upload-instructions.pdf and s3-presign-policy.txt.

Operational notes:
- Please include a human-readable "who_uploaded" field in the manifest (email), and attach the KMS signature block. That's what auditors look for.
- We'll also create audit-checksum.txt with filename -> SHA256 -> objectVersionId. That file will be part of the manifest and copied into the OneTrust evidence field as a single attachment.

Marissa — looping you for final confirmation on the 2-hour upload window and to coordinate Redwood CS presence during intake.

Ben
Security Integrations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: upload-instructions.pdf, s3-presign-policy.txt

- Share the Greenfield intake endpoints for OneTrust and Vendr and any required field names (we map them into the manifest).
- Attach the actual artifacts to upload or provide a short list with filenames and expected sizes.
- If you can, reply with a single approval email so our compliance team can reference it in the manifest.

After the upload we'll provide:
- signed-manifest.json (KMS-signed, SHA256 inventory)
- audit-checksum.txt (filename -> SHA256 -> S3 version id)
- a short intake ticket summary for your auditors.

Thanks — Marissa Cole
